name: TRELLIS.2
paper_title: Native and Compact Structured Latents for 3D Generation
license_interpretation: The TRELLIS.2 code and its microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B weights are MIT, a permissive license that allows commercial and closed-source use with the copyright notice kept. The image encoder it needs is not: facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m is Meta's, under the DINOv3 License, a custom agreement that is not OSI-approved. It permits redistribution with a copy of the agreement and passes through trade-control and end-use restrictions (military, weapons, espionage and nuclear uses among them), so it sets the terms for the pipeline as a whole; read it before shipping a product on it. LibreYOLO's adapter is MIT, and the flow models, VAE decoder and dual-grid meshing it adapts from TRELLIS.2 keep MIT, noted in libreyolo/models/gen/trellis2/NOTICE. Upstream's nvdiffrast and nvdiffrec (NVIDIA, non-commercial) and BRIA's RMBG-2.0 (non-commercial) are not used, and the texture stage is not ported. Weights are redistributed unchanged at pinned revisions and none is gated: the geometry networks as LibreYOLO/LibreTRELLIS2-4b, TRELLIS's structure decoder and the BiRefNet weights (MIT) from LibreYOLO/LibreTRELLISl, and the DINOv3 encoder as LibreYOLO/LibreDINOv3vitl16 with the agreement.
